# Positive-control corpus — codepoint/description table

`corpus.yaml` is the positive-control corpus for the untrusted-read sample corpus: the
shared library of known-bad (and known-good) samples every detector layer proves itself
against. No layer may trust a clean report until it has demonstrated it FLAGS a known-bad
sample, and the benign entries prove it does not cry wolf on clean input.

## The table is a specification, not a payload store

The tree carries a **codepoint / description table**, never a decoded attack string. Each
entry lists the codepoint sequence *by value* (e.g. `U+E0001`), and the generator
(`untrustcorpus.Load`) assembles the UTF-8 bytes **in memory at run time**. Nothing
committed here is itself a payload, which is why the table can be authored and reviewed by
eye where the decoded samples could not. The table itself contains no invisible or bidi
character — it names them.

## Schema

Top-level key `entries`, a list. Each entry:

| field | meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `id` | stable identifier, unique within the table |
| `class` | `exfil-callout` \| `injection-unicode` \| `injection-imperative` \| `code-exec` \| `install-hook` \| `benign` |
| `layer` | the detector layer this entry is a positive control for: `A` (the deterministic scan) or `B/D` (the no-egress sandbox) |
| `codepoints` | the ordered codepoint sequence the generator assembles, each as `U+XXXX` (1–6 hex digits) |
| `description` | what shape the generator builds and why a scanner should flag (or, for benign, ignore) it |
| `expect` | `{scan: flag\|clean, reason: <marker>}` — the deterministic-scan verdict; `reason` is the marker a consumer asserts on |
| `sha256` | pin over the generated UTF-8 bytes; the reproducibility test asserts it |

Detector layers are fixed by the stream scope: `A` and `B/D` only. There is **no
model-read layer** — the narrower stream scope removed it — so no entry may name one, and
a validator rejects any other value. Every layer that exists must be named by at least one
entry (an orphaned layer has no proof it sees its own fault class), and every entry must
name a layer (an entry naming no layer is a fixture with no consumer).

## Generator contract

`untrustcorpus.Load(dir)` reads `<dir>/corpus.yaml` and returns `[]Sample{ID, Class,
Layer, Bytes, Expect, SHA256}`. The assembler is a **pure codepoint decoder**: it maps
each `U+XXXX` token to a Unicode scalar value and appends its UTF-8 encoding, in order.
It has **no clock, no randomness, no map-iteration-order dependence, and no
locale-dependent encoding**, so the same table produces byte-identical output on every
platform and every run. Surrogates and out-of-range values are rejected.

Reproducibility is hash-pinned: for every entry `sha256(generated bytes)` must equal the
entry's `sha256` (`TestReproducible`), and a one-bit perturbation must break the pin
(`TestReproducible_PerturbationIsCaught`). Inertness is asserted over the generated bytes:
no live callout host, no `ghp_`/`ghs_`/`github_pat_` credential shape, no non-loopback
external host (`TestGeneratedSamplesAreInert`). Every sink resolves to `example.invalid` /
a loopback address; every credential is a placeholder or an env-var name.

The harness READS generated bytes; it NEVER executes them.

## Adding an entry

1. Author the **shape**, not a payload. Decide the codepoint sequence — for the unicode
   classes this is literally the codepoints; for the structural classes (exfil, code-exec,
   install-hook) express the inert shape as its codepoints, keeping every sink at
   `example.invalid` / loopback and every credential a placeholder.
2. Compute the pin: `sha256` of the assembled UTF-8 bytes. Run `untrustcorpus list` to see
   the assembled byte length, and `untrustcorpus check` to validate structure.
3. Name the `layer` this entry is a positive control for, and set `expect`.
4. Run the package tests — `TestReproducible`, `TestGeneratedSamplesAreInert`, and, for a
   unicode entry, `TestGeneratesInvisibleUnicode` (the discriminator: the generated bytes
   must actually contain Tag-block / zero-width / bidi codepoints — describing smuggling
   is not enough).

## Validating

```
go run ./cmd/untrustcorpus check          # structural validation; prints "corpus-ok"
go run ./cmd/untrustcorpus list           # per-entry id/class/layer/verdict/byte-length
go test ./internal/deskkit/untrustcorpus/ # reproducibility, inertness, discriminator
```

The root is **derived, not typed**: `--root` overrides, else `ASSAY_UNTRUST_CORPUS_ROOT`,
else the shipped in-repo location.
